name: Dingo
description: Dingo is a strategic card game for four players from Cleveland, Ohio. The game features a unique 'hunt' mechanic where diamonds (rabbits) are hunted in ascending order, with hearts (dingoes) and black cards (wolves) playing special roles. Players score points based on card values and hunt outcomes.

setup.players:
Minimum Players: 4
Maximum Players: 4
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: None - individual play
setup.deck:
Type: Standard 52-card deck with special classifications
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included
Special classifications:
- Diamonds = 'rabbits' (Ace of diamonds = 'Ace rabbit')
- Hearts = 'dingoes'
- Spades and Clubs = 'wolves'
setup.dealing:
First dealer chosen randomly, passes left after each game
Dealer separates diamonds from deck (except Ace of diamonds stays in main pack)
Diamonds 2-K ordered low to high, placed face up in center (2 on top)
Main pack: 40 cards (13 hearts, 13 spades, 13 clubs, 1 Ace of diamonds)
Shuffle and deal 10 cards to each player
setup.equipment:
Standard 52-card deck
Table space for rabbit pile and discards
Score sheet

rules.objective: Score as many points as possible by the end of the game through the hunt phase.
rules.gameplay:
DISCARD AND EXCHANGE PHASE (reduces hand from 10 to 6 cards):
1. First Discard: Each player discards one card face up (Aces cannot be discarded)
2. First Exchange (Left): Pass one card face down to left
3. Second Discard: Everyone discards again
4. Second Exchange (Across): Pass one card to player opposite
5. Third Discard: Everyone discards again
6. Third Exchange (Right): Pass one card to right
7. Fourth Discard: Final discard, leaving 6 cards each

THE HUNT PHASE:
Rabbits hunted in ascending order (2 through King, then Ace)
Dealer calls rank, holder of dingo (heart) of that rank must play it
Other players may play wolves (spades/clubs) of that rank:
- No dingo: Rabbit discarded, no score
- Dingo but no wolves: Dingo goes to penalty pile
- Dingo and one wolf: Dingo to scoring pile, wolf player catches rabbit
- Dingo and both wolves: First wolf and dingo to dingo player's scoring pile, second wolf catches rabbit

ACE HUNT (special rules):
All Aces must be in players' hands (cannot be discarded)
Dingo player plays Ace dingo, then each player in turn may play Ace wolves
Ace rabbit can only be played if both Ace wolves already played
Scoring based on which Aces are played
keyRules: Aces can never be discarded during exchange phase
Dingo holder must play dingo when rank is called
Only players other than dingo player can play wolves
Ace rabbit can only be played after both Ace wolves played
Never sensible to play both wolves if you hold both (first wolf scores for dingo player)
Cards have different values in scoring vs penalty piles

strategy.basic:
Manage your hand through discards and exchanges to keep valuable cards
Understand when to play wolves during hunts
Avoid being stuck with negative cards in penalty pile
strategy.intermediate:
Strategic discarding to shape your hand for hunts
Evaluate when to play wolves based on potential rabbit capture
Manage Ace cards carefully for final hunt
strategy.advanced:
Reading opponents' discards and exchanges for information
Complex wolf play timing
Ace hunt endgame strategy
Probability calculations for wolf distribution
tips: Never discard Aces - they cannot be replaced
If you hold both wolves of a rank, never play both (first helps dingo player)
Watch what cards opponents pass during exchanges
Ace rabbit is very valuable (+10) but risky (-3 if stuck)
Plan your 6-card hand carefully for the hunt phase

scoring.description: Score is value of scoring pile minus value of penalty pile after disqualification checks.
scoring.winCondition: Highest valid score at game end wins; ties are broken by highest live rabbit captured.
